svg.aria-label: Credit Risk Underwriting Engine architecture: raw loan tape to bronze Delta, through a Unity Catalog leakage firewall that blocks post-origination columns, into LightGBM training with out-of-time validation, isotonic calibration, expected-value pricing and SHAP explainability, then MLflow pyfunc packaging, Databricks Model Serving, Lakehouse drift monitoring and a guarded text2sql agent.
svg.text: 1.35M loans · leakage-safe PD model · governed on the lakehouse
CC0 · landed in a UC Volume
every leakage column is kept here
blocked · recoveries · total_pymnt · last_fico_range_* · settlement · hardship
a single whitelist CREATE TABLE AS SELECT — no post-origination column reaches a feature
field reaches a feature — and the run
asserts it, so a breach fails the build
Databricks on AWS — Unity Catalog tables are
Delta files in S3, notebooks run on EC2
the same notebook runs on Free Edition
MODEL PLANE · TRAIN → CALIBRATE → PRICE → EXPLAIN

g.text: random K-fold flatters a credit model —
it will be deployed on future vintages
one MLflow run · params, metrics, artifacts
so the ranking is left untouched
a probability is not a decision — the cutoff
is set by economics, not by F1
term interest earned vs 65% LGD loss
ECOA obliges a lender to say why — so a
reason code ships with every score
signed, pinned and versioned as one artifact
the inference log is the substrate — predicted PD
against realized default, profiled by vintage
newer vintages default above forecast — the very
drift stage 02 corrects, now caught on its own
every figure it states comes from a tool call —
it is never permitted to estimate a PD itself
single statement · SELECT only · table whitelist
row cap · 11/11 injection + DDL attacks blocked

svg.text: PROVE THE FIREWALL · JUDGE ON FUTURE VINTAGES · PRICE THE DECISION · EXPLAIN EVERY DECLINE
